qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Dense local route networks across ~800 North American and global branches minimize technician drive time while ~81-85% recurring contract retention, food/pharma compliance lock-in, and PestConnect IoT deter rivals. Empirically, gross margins held 83.0%-83.5% (FY23-FY25) with >100% Tangible Operating ROIC (~$390M tangible IC vs $6.9B sales) and consistent inflation+ price realization (International pest organic growth +5.7% in Q3 2026). Primary erosion threats: GAAP ROIC depressed to 5.1%-6.9% by $8.9B Terminix M&A goodwill/intangibles, and NA pest organic growth (2.4%-2.6% in H1/Q3 2026) still trailing Rollins while recovering from 2023-2024 branch integration disruption.
qualitative.calamity_note: (1) Broken gates/metrics: Raw Gate 5 (0) and Gate 6 (N) failures from legacy management's $6.7B Terminix M&A blunder (GAAP ROIC 5.1%-6.9% vs 12% hurdle; ~$412M gap between FY25 Adjusted Operating Profit $1,070M and statutory Operating Income $658M / EBIT $640M from integration charges & $201M FY25 / $47M H1 26 termite provisions; retired 2027 20% NA margin target in Jul/Oct 2026) and leverage/coverage strain (statutory EBIT/Interest 2.56x < 5.0x, LT Debt/NI 8.8x, Net Debt $3.58B / FCF ~$615M ~5.8x > 4.0x, -$3.42B tangible equity, $392M termite provision costing $115M-$125M/yr cash in 2026). (2) Intact route-density moat & customer unit economics: Core asset-light route engine is unharmed—FY25 gross margin stayed 83.1%, Tangible Operating ROIC >100%, adjusted FCF conversion 96%-98% ($615M FY25; $318M H1 26), International pest organic growth accelerated to +5.7% (Q3 2026), group customer retention rose ~100 bps in H1 2026, colleague retention climbed to 82.2%, and NA pest organic growth rebounded sequentially from 0.1% (H1 25) to 2.4%-2.6% (Q4 25-Q3 26) once forced branch/ERP mergers were paused. (3) Concrete turnaround catalyst & kill-switch: Trian Partners (~2.26% stake, Brian Baldwin on Board Oct 2024) catalyzed leadership reset to U.S. route-logistics veteran CEO Mike Duffy (March 2026), Branch 360 BI rollout without ERP rip-and-replace, ~800 branches (~220 satellites), NA Residential/Commercial split, France Workwear (EUR 410M EV) & SOLitude ($230M) disposals, and Net Debt/Adj. EBITDA compression from 2.9x (FY24) to 2.4x (H1 26). Kill-switch: by FY2027 results (Feb 2028), NA Pest organic growth must reach >=4.0%, statutory continuing-ops Owner EPS must exceed the 2023 peak ($0.192) as special charges sunset, and Net Debt/EBITDA must hold <=2.2x with termite cash claims <=$125M/yr, or permanently reject.
qualitative.note: Calamity pass (Anchor Gates 1, 2, 3a, 4 pass; raw Gate 5=0 and Gate 6=N waived as fixable integration/deleveraging calamity). Global #1 route-density pest control & hygiene compounder (~85% pest mix post-Workwear) insulated from AI disruption (15Y CAP) with 83.1% gross margins, >100% Tangible Operating ROIC, and 96%-98% adjusted FCF conversion. Turnaround under Trian board oversight and new US CEO Mike Duffy is restoring NA organic growth (2.4%-2.6%) and lowering Net Debt/EBITDA to 2.4x, though statutory 2.56x interest cover and $392M legacy termite claims require monitoring until the Feb 2028 kill-switch. [5-10Y g: pest volume 2.0% + price 2.5% + NA recovery/mix 1.0% - termite/reinvestment drag 0.5% + buybacks/deleveraging 0.5%]
qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle financials: Pre-Terminix GAAP ROIC was 9.4%-12.6% (2018-2021) before the Oct 2022 $6.7B Terminix acquisition added $6.58B goodwill and $2.33B intangibles, depressing FY22-FY25 GAAP ROIC to 4.0%-6.7% (4Y median 6.90%; FY25 5.1% on statutory EBIT $640M) while Tangible Operating ROIC stayed >100% (~$390M tangible IC). Gross margins held steady at 81.0% (FY22), 83.0% (FY23), 83.5% (FY24), and 83.1% (FY25). Statutory EBIT moved from $798M (FY23) to $705M (FY24) to $640M (FY25), while Adjusted Operating Profit reached $1,070M (+5.4% cc, 15.5% margin) in FY25 and $556M (+6.6% cc, 15.5% margin) in H1 2026; continuing-ops Net Income fell $437M->$346M->$290M (FY23-FY25; total FY25 NI $470M boosted by $180M Workwear discontinued ops). Cash flow conversion remains strong: Yahoo FCF was $496M (FY22), $654M (FY23), $593M (FY24), and $703M (FY25; 151% 4Y FCF/GAAP NI on $269M capex vs $563M D&A); company adjusted FCF was $615M (98% conversion) in FY25 and $318M (96% conversion) in H1 2026. Segment/regional mix & turnaround: Post-France Workwear disposal (EUR 410M EV closed Sep 2025, saving $93M/yr capex) and pending SOLitude Lake Management sale ($230M EV / ~$180M net proceeds, Sep 2026), group revenue ($6,908M FY25) is ~85% Pest Control and ~15% Hygiene & Wellbeing (~62% North America). Group organic growth rose from 2.6% FY25 (1.6% H1 -> 3.5% H2) to 3.6% H1 2026 and 3.4% Q3 2026; NA Pest Control organic growth improved from 0.1% (H1 25) to 1.8% (Q3 25), 2.6% (Q4 25 & H1 26), and 2.4% (Q3 26), while International Pest reached 5.7% in Q3 2026. Pausing forced branch/IT consolidation in 2025, deploying Branch 360 across ~30 heritage brands and ~800 branches (~220 satellites), splitting NA Residential/Commercial (Q3 2026), and retiring the 2027 20% NA margin target (Jul/Oct 2026) lifted group customer retention ~100 bps in H1 2026 and colleague retention to 82.2%. Balance sheet & claims: FY25 Total Debt $6,130M (LT Debt $4,156M), Cash $2,319M, company Net Debt $3,650M (FY25) -> $3,575M (H1 26), Net Debt/Adj. EBITDA improved 2.9x (FY24) -> 2.6x (FY25) -> 2.4x (H1 26); however, FY25 statutory EBIT/Interest is 2.56x ($640M/$250M), LT Debt/NI is 8.8x, legacy termite claims provision stands at $392M (H1 26; $201M FY25 + $47M H1 26 charges; $95M cash settled FY25, $115M-$125M guided FY26), and a $200M buyback was launched in H1 2026.
